text: Azure SQL already protects PolicyClaimsDB against a local hardware failure automatically. Protecting it against losing an entire Azure region is a separate job, and it has to be built on purpose.

Layer one, built-in HA with zone redundancy, needs no setup at all. Layer two, cross-region DR, means an explicit secondary server and an auto-failover group -- apps connect through the group's listener, never the primary server's hostname directly.
The failover group pairs thornridge-sql-server with a secondary server in a different region. That listener detail matters: it's what silently redirects traffic after a real failover.
We're setting explicit recovery targets now, and committing in writing to a real failover drill once this is built -- because an HA and DR plan nobody has ever actually tested is only a hypothesis.
Resilience is planned on paper. Next: opening Terraform and turning three lessons of planning into the real Azure SQL environment.
